Title: GSMC welcomes new cohort of Masters' students
NewsSummary: The school welcomed the fourth Cohort of the Masters in Digital Journalism Programme.

content.text: The Graduate School of Media and Communications welcomed the fourth Cohort of the Masters in Digital Journalism Programme. The new cohort has 37 students drawn from Kenya and Uganda.
Our team met with one of the student's, Eve Masawi, who shared her enthusiasm for joining the programme.
Why did you pick journalism as a career?

Ever since I was a little girl, it was evident to those around me that I was very curious. I had the hunger to know and learn more. I wanted to be the go-to person for all the facts, the one who told all the amazing stories. With age grew the passion for knowledge, and so did the desire to make it available to those who need it and to tell the stories of those who needed a voice but have little access.  This is the reason I joined active journalism.
You are starting a new journey amidst a pandemic, what does this mean to you?

To me this means hope. This pandemic has taught me not to live in despair, Why? - Because even during tough times there is always a ray of hope. Who am I to have gotten this course, something I never saw coming? Especially since a number of my colleagues and friends have lost their jobs and loved ones because of the pandemic. In addition people struggling financially because the economy has been greatly affected. I will, therefore, describe this as "HOPE".
What are your expectations from the programme?
I expect to unlearn the practical and be open to learning even more and more.
I expect to share my experience with my classmates and others
I expect to learn from others because I believe they come with different skills and experience.
I expect to enrich the virtue of giving without expecting.
I expect to enrich my social environment since I will be meeting people from different countries and media houses.
I also expect to learn from the best. I know for a fact that Aga Khan University is known for its great sources and quality education.

Eve Masawi is a digital journalist with a zeal for unique insights into original stories. Coupled with strong editorial judgment, fervent skill, and wit, Eve has since childhood believed that her story is one that is worth telling to the world. She holds a Bachelor's Degree in Mass Communication from Uganda Christian University. Her recent work as a Digital Journalist with the African Institute for Investigative Journalism, NBS TV/Next Media Services and formerly NTV, have been a stepping stone for this young and riveting talent. Eve exudes charm and aggressiveness even as a reporter.
